title: Where Does the Performance Go? Understanding and Recovering Performance Regressions in C-to-Rust Translation
abstract: arXiv:2610.23044v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Rust is increasingly adopted as a memory-safe successor to C, and transpilers such as \crust{} can migrate entire C projects while preserving their behavior. Preserving behavior, however, does not guarantee preserving performance. We study this gap on 20 real-world C projects and their \crust{} translations. On the eight projects used for analysis, the translated Rust is more than 3\% slower than the original C on 12 of 19 operations, by up to 62.2\%. By comparing execution-cost profiles, optimized LLVM IR, and compiler optimization remarks across each C--Rust pair, we trace these slowdowns to nine recurring performance issues, spanning residual runtime work, missed compiler optimizations, and C-style source patterns, and derive an optimization direction for each. We then present \ourtool{}, an LLM-based approach that encodes these issues as reusable optimization rules to recover the performance of translated Rust. \ourtool{} profiles ea

translated_title: 性能去哪了？理解并恢复 C 到 Rust 转换中的性能退化
translated_abstract: Rust 正日益被采纳为 C 语言的内存安全继任者，而像 C2Rust 这样的自动转换器可以在保持程序行为不变的前提下迁移完整的 C 项目。然而，保持行为并不意味着保持性能。本文在 20 个真实世界的 C 项目及其 C2Rust 转换版本上研究了这一差距。在用于分析的八个项目中，转换后的 Rust 在 19 个操作中有 12 个比原始 C 代码慢超过 3%，最严重时慢达 62.2%。通过对比每对 C--Rust 程序的执行成本剖析、优化后的 LLVM IR 以及编译器优化备注，作者将这些性能下降追溯到九类反复出现的性能问题，涵盖残留的运行时开销、错失的编译器优化以及 C 风格的源代码模式，并为每类问题推导出相应的优化方向。随后，作者提出了一种基于大语言模型（LLM）的方法，将这些性能问题编码为可重用的优化规则，以恢复转换后 Rust 代码的性能。该工具会对程序进行剖析……
tldr: 该论文系统性地研究了 C 到 Rust 自动转换造成的性能退化问题，通过对执行剖析、LLVM IR 和编译器优化备注的对比分析识别出九类反复出现的性能问题，并提出了一种基于 LLM 的工具，将这些问题编码为可重用的优化规则来恢复转换后 Rust 代码的性能。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically investigates performance regressions caused by automated C-to-Rust translation, identifies nine recurring performance issues through comparative analysis of execution-cost profiles, optimized LLVM IR, and compiler optimization remarks, and proposes an LLM-based tool that encodes these issues as reusable optimization rules to recover the performance of translated Rust code.
